summary: @tag_pattern/@indent_pattern (built at lines 16-17) use Ruby's `^` line-anchor instead of `\A` string-anchor, so an embedded `//`-looking line deep inside a Go `/* ... */` multi-line block comment is misdetected as a tag or continuation line.
README.md:47 advertises Go TODOs supporting both `//` and `/* */` comment syntax, but `comment_marker` is hardcoded to `"//"` only, so a `/* TODO(...) */` block-style tag is never recognized.
failure_scenario: Reproduced: `CommentParser.parse("/* TODO(on: date('2024-06-01'), to: 'dev@example.com')\n   Remove this. */\n", adapter: Go)` returns 0 todos — the feature the PR's own documentation promises does not work, with no error surfaced.

summary: adapter_for raises an uncaught ArgumentError for any explicitly-named file whose extension isn't .rb/.py/.go (including no extension), crashing the whole CLI run — a regression from the old code which scanned any explicit file as Ruby regardless of extension.
failure_scenario: Reproduced: `smart_todo smart_todo.gemspec ...` now raises `ArgumentError: No SmartTodo source adapter registered for "smart_todo.gemspec"` and aborts; previously this worked. Same crash hits Rakefile, Gemfile, bin/console, config.ru, *.rake — common real-world invocations.

summary: The except clause wraps the whole tokenize loop, but `tokenize.detect_encoding()` raises that same SyntaxError before yielding any tokens when the file's first two lines contain a byte invalid for the assumed encoding (no PEP263 cookie) — silently dropping ALL comments in the file.
failure_scenario: Reproduced with python3 directly: a .py file with a Latin-1 accented byte on line 1/2 and no coding cookie causes `tokenize.tokenize()` to raise `SyntaxError: invalid or missing encoding declaration` immediately; the script's broad except swallows it and prints `[]`. A perfectly valid `# TODO(...)` anywhere in that file is silently never scanned, with zero error reported.

summary: SourceAdapters::Python::Error (e.g. python3 missing from PATH, or a non-zero tokenizer exit) propagates uncaught out of parse_file/CLI#run instead of following this class's usual @errors-accumulation/exit-1 pattern.
failure_scenario: With python3 absent from PATH, scanning any .py file raises `Python::Error: python3 is required...` uncaught, crashing the entire scan (including already-processed Ruby/Go files' pending dispatches) with a raw backtrace instead of a graceful exit code 1.

summary: When no comment/string/rune regex matches, the scanner falls back to consuming one character at a time, so content inside an unterminated/malformed Go string literal is re-scanned char-by-char and a stray `//` inside it is misidentified as a real comment.
failure_scenario: Reproduced: `s := "unterminated string with a // TODO(on: date('2024-06-01'), to: 'dev@example.com')` (missing closing quote) causes `Go.extract_comments` to return the embedded `// TODO(...)` text as a genuine comment, which then parses into a fully live, false-positive Todo with real metadata pulled from string content.

summary: Go.extract_comments has no rescue for invalid byte sequences; StringScanner#scan raises ArgumentError on non-UTF-8-valid source, uncaught anywhere up the call chain.
failure_scenario: Scanning a .go file containing any byte invalid for UTF-8 (e.g. a Latin-1/Windows-1252 string literal) makes `scanner.scan(LINE_COMMENT)` raise `ArgumentError: invalid byte sequence in UTF-8`, propagating uncaught through CLI#run and crashing the entire multi-file scan, not just the offending file.

summary: LINE_COMMENT (`%r{//[^\n]*}`) excludes only `\n`, not `\r`, so on CRLF-encoded Go source a trailing carriage return is captured as part of the comment text and ends up embedded in the Todo's comment body.
failure_scenario:
Reproduced: a CRLF Go file (`"// TODO(...)
//   Remove this.
"`) yields `todo.comment == "Remove this.
"` with an embedded ``, corrupting the notification message. Ruby/Python paths have no equivalent gap.

summary: glob_pattern only globs `extensions.first`, while `SourceAdapters.for_extension` checks the whole `extensions` array — a latent inconsistency that would silently under-scan directories for any future adapter declaring 2+ extensions.
failure_scenario: Reproduced with a synthetic adapter declaring `extensions => [".foo", ".bar"]`: directory scan finds `a.foo` but never `b.bar`, while `smart_todo dir/b.bar` (explicit file) is picked up fine via adapter_for. Currently dormant only because Ruby/Python/Go each declare exactly one extension.

summary: extract_comments shells out to a brand-new python3 process for every single Python file scanned, with no batching.
failure_scenario: Scanning a repo with hundreds of .py files spawns hundreds of sequential CPython interpreter startups on the hot scanning path; batching multiple files into one python3 invocation would pay interpreter-boot cost once instead of N times.

summary: Todo#initialize independently re-derives Regexp.escape(marker) and indent-measuring logic that CommentParser already computed once per adapter in @indent_pattern, duplicating the same marker-parsing rule in two classes.
failure_scenario: Any future marker-format quirk (tabs, no required space, multi-char markers) must be fixed in both lib/smart_todo/comment_parser.rb:17 and lib/smart_todo/todo.rb:12, and the two could silently disagree on what counts as valid indent.

summary: for_extension reimplements a 'map key to one of a fixed set of Classes' registry via Array#find, duplicating the class-dispatch pattern already established by Dispatchers::Base.class_for elsewhere in the same codebase.
failure_scenario: The codebase now has two different styles for the same problem (dispatcher lookup via case-statement vs adapter lookup via Array#find+include?), making the pattern harder to find/reuse consistently as more adapters or dispatchers are added.

summary: normalize_path issues 3 separate full-tree Dir[] globs (one per registered adapter) and then flat_maps/sorts, instead of one combined brace-glob pattern.
failure_scenario: On a large repo, each of `Dir["#{path}/**/*.rb"]`, `**/*.py`, `**/*.go` independently walks the whole directory tree, tripling filesystem traversal cost per path argument versus a single `Dir["#{path}/**/*.{rb,py,go}"]`.

summary: adapter_for raises a bare, uncaught ArgumentError instead of routing into the established @errors-accumulation/exit-code convention used for every other error path in this class.
failure_scenario: One unsupported file among many valid ones (e.g. a pre-commit hook running `smart_todo $(git diff --name-only)`, which often includes README.md/Gemfile.lock alongside .rb files) aborts the entire run with a raw backtrace instead of a reported error and exit code 1, discarding all TODOs already found earlier in the same loop.

summary: No test exercises a Go block comment TODO end-to-end through CommentParser/CLI; test_extracts_block_comments only checks raw extraction of a non-tagged block comment.
failure_scenario: The corruption/truncation/silent-drop bugs above (multi-line block comments breaking CommentParser's line-anchored regexes) shipped completely unexercised by the test suite, and would only surface when a real user writes a Go TODO inside a `/* */` doc comment.
